pins.claim: / is IEEE on zero divisors: 1/0 = inf, 0/0 = NaN, 1/-0.0 = -inf (Spark ANSI and BigQuery's bare / both ERROR here - forced in the printers)
// and % return NULL on a zero divisor (Spark ANSI and BigQuery DIV/MOD error - guarded in the printers)
INT_MIN % -1 is an overflow trap at every width (Spark and BigQuery MOD return 0 - forced back into an error in the printers)
pins.observed: ERROR: Out of Range Error: Overflow in division of -9223372036854775808 / -1 | ERROR: Out of Range Error: Overflow in division of -2147483648 / -1

pins.claim: CAST DOUBLE -> INTEGER rounds half-even, never truncates (Spark truncates - forced via rint)
pins.query: SELECT CAST(2.7::DOUBLE AS INTEGER), CAST(2.5::DOUBLE AS INTEGER), CAST(1.5::DOUBLE AS INTEGER), CAST((-2.5)::DOUBLE AS INTEGER)

pins.claim: CAST DECIMAL -> INTEGER rounds half-AWAY-from-zero (Spark truncates - forced via round)
pins.query: SELECT CAST(2.5::DECIMAL(3,1) AS INTEGER), CAST((-2.5)::DECIMAL(3,1) AS INTEGER), CAST(2.4::DECIMAL(3,1) AS INTEGER)

pins.claim: CAST '1.5' (string) -> INTEGER parses and ROUNDS; Spark treats it as malformed (string-source casts refuse in the printers)
pins.query: SELECT CAST('1.5' AS INTEGER), TRY_CAST('1.5' AS INTEGER)

pins.claim: Floats order TOTALLY: NaN equals NaN and exceeds everything (BigQuery comparisons are IEEE - forced with IS_NAN cases)
Decimal literal typing counts a bare-zero integer part as one digit: typeof(0.5) = DECIMAL(2,1)
FLOAT / FLOAT computes at FLOAT, not DOUBLE (the plan refuses f32 division rather than derive a wrong width)
